title: From Bengaluru's Basavanagudi to Adobe CEO: Anil Chakravarthy to steer software giant in the AI era- Moneycontrol.com
text:

September 05, 2026 / 10:54 IST             Anil Chakravarthy, a veteran Adobe leader who grew up in India’s tech capital Bengaluru, is set to join the growing ranks of Indian-origin executives leading some of the world’s most influential technology companies. Yesterday, Chakravarthy was  named as Adobe’s next president and chief executive officer , replacing long-time CEO Shantanu Narayen, who announced plans to  step down earlier this year . Chakravarthy, who currently serves as president of Adobe's Customer Experience Orchestration business, will take over the role on December 1, 2026. Narayen, who led the company for more than 18 years, will transition to executive chair and "work closely" with Chakravarthy during the transition period, the company said. Chakravarthy joins a growing group of global tech leaders from Karnataka, including  Rahul Patil , CTO of Anthropic; Sachin Katti, who leads OpenAI’s infrastructure and compute strategy; and Amar Subramanya, Vice President of AI at Apple. The move comes as the design software maker seeks to navigate rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and growing competition from AI-powered rivals such as Canva, as well as tools developed by AI research labs including Anthropic and OpenAI, as businesses increasingly embrace agentic AI systems. From South Bengaluru to Silicon Valley Chakravarthy grew up in South Bengaluru, one of the city’s oldest and most storied parts. After completing high school in Jayanagar's Vijaya High School, and his pre-university studies in Basavanagudi's National College between 1983 to 1985, he moved to Varanasi to study computer science at the Institute of Technology, Banaras Hindu University. At the age of 21, he moved to the United States to pursue further studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), where he went on to earn a master’s degree and PhD, completing his doctorate in 1995. Chakravarthy later described this period as the time when he "went from being an aspiring scientist to an aspiring businessman." He started his professional career at McKinsey and also worked at companies like Logictier and VeriSign. Chakravarthy spent nearly a decade at Symantec from 2004 to 2013, rising through the ranks to become executive vice president of Information Security. During his stint, he oversaw engineering, product management and operations for a wide-ranging security product portfolio. In a 2017 CNBC podcast, Chakravarthy recalled that he first realised he wanted to become a CEO when he was an engineering leader at Symantec. Then-CEO John Thompson placed him in a role managing services to see if he could do it. The experience pushed him beyond his engineering comfort zone and became a defining moment in his journey towards aiming for a leadership role. "That's when I started to say, I should get a variety of different types of experiences. One thing led to another – that's how I ended up at Informatica as chief product officer," he said. He joined enterprise cloud data management firm Informatica as executive vice president and chief product officer in 2013 and became its CEO in 2015, a role he held until 2020. Chakravarthy's rise at Adobe Chakravarthy met Shantanu Narayen through Informatica’s relationship with Adobe, wherein the company was a partner of the Adobe Experience Platform, particularly in the data integration space. "A lot of the reason I came was the opportunity to work with him and work with the leadership team at Adobe," he said in a CNBC interview in 2021. Chakravarthy joined Adobe in January 2020 as executive vice president and general manager leading the company's Digital Experience business. In September 2020, he took on the additional responsibility of leading the company’s worldwide field operations, serving enterprise customers across Adobe’s full portfolio of products, including creativity and productivity. In December 2021, he was promoted to president of Digital Experience and worldwide field operations. Under Chakravarthy’s leadership, Adobe has become a market leader in Customer Experience Orchestration solutions, which helps businesses use real-time data and AI to deliver more personalised customer experiences across digital channels. The sector has become particularly important as customer experiences are changing rapidly across digital channels and AI surfaces, requiring companies to better manage interactions across platforms and deliver more consistent experiences. Businesses are also turning to AI agents to accelerate complex workflows, from on-brand content production to one-to-one personalisation. Chakravarthy has led the development of AI-powered and agentic customer experience products including  Adobe CX Enterprise, GenStudio and Brand Visibility . He has also helped scale the Adobe Experience Platform and drive new product innovations such as CX Enterprise Coworker. Chakravarthy also played a key role in Adobe’s acquisitions of Workfront and  Semrush  and their subsequent integration into the company’s portfolio. Narayen said that Chakravarthy has a "proven record of building and delivering category-defining products" that serves the software firm's broad range of customers. “I could not be more confident that Anil is the right person to lead Adobe's growth in an AI-driven era,” he said. India a key hub for Adobe India is  home to Adobe's largest workforce  outside the United States, with more than 8,500 employees across five campuses including Bengaluru, Noida, Gurugram, Mumbai,and Hyderabad. In 2025, the company announced plans to expand its footprint with a new campus in Noida, its third in Uttar Pradesh. The software firm, which entered India in 1997, says it was the  first global tech company  to run an entire business from the country, including research and development centres that develop many of its products. Teams in India contribute to more than a third of Adobe’s innovation efforts across its three cloud businesses — creative cloud, document cloud, and experience cloud. Product development for several key Adobe products, including the illustration software Illustrator and Acrobat PDF software, is led by these teams. “I could not be more confident that Anil is the right person to lead Adobe's growth in an AI-driven era,” he said.

India a key hub for Adobe

India is home to Adobe's largest workforce outside the United States, with more than 8,500 employees across five campuses including Bengaluru, Noida, Gurugram, Mumbai,and Hyderabad. In 2025, the company announced plans to expand its footprint with a new campus in Noida, its third in Uttar Pradesh.

The software firm, which entered India in 1997, says it was the first global tech company to run an entire business from the country, including research and development centres that develop many of its products.
